Pool-host leasing now quarantines dead hosts instead of retrying them forever. A row whose lease-time SSH key injection fails is flipped to status `unreachable` (committed, logged at error level) and the lease immediately retries the next-oldest matching row, bounded at 3 attempts per request. Previously the failed transaction rolled back and every lease re-selected the same dead row, which blocked all workspace creation during the 2026-08-07 production incident (a box whose NVMe drive died). When quarantining drains the pool the caller gets the standard no-capacity 503; when the per-request attempt cap is hit it gets a retryable 502 naming the quarantined count.

The hourly slice-reconcile cron now also probes each bare-metal box's hardware health over the same management SSH: a degraded md RAID array (from `/proc/mdstat`) or an unmirrored raw-partition swap device (from `/proc/swaps`) is logged at error level and counted as a divergence. Both signals are the precursor state of the 2026-08-07 incident, which previously ran undetected for six days.
